prompt: You ask an agent to "clean up this function" and it also renames three variables in a file you didn't mention. Which lens do you read that through?

options.label: "It did something wrong" (verify-everything lens)
options.content: Every future request now gets the same suspicious full re-read, regardless of task size. You end up re-deriving the work yourself to check it, which erases most of the time delegating was supposed to save - and you still haven't learned anything about why it happened.

options.label: "That's scope creep" (categorized lens)
options.content: You recognize the pattern: it treated "clean up" as license to touch anything nearby. Fix is narrow and specific - name the exact file and function next time - and future requests in that shape get exactly that boundary, while everything else stays at normal trust. One data point, correctly filed, instead of a permanent tax on every future request.
